request: why does a compass needle point north?

beats.intent: The Earth drawn as a circle with a giant bar magnet inside it
beats.narration: The Earth behaves as if it had a giant bar magnet inside.
beats.code:
stage.title("Why compasses point north")
earth = Circle(radius=2.2, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.25).move_to([-2.5, -0.3, 0])
magnet_s = Rectangle(width=0.5, height=1.2, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.9).move_to(earth.get_center() + 0.6 * UP)
magnet_n = Rectangle(width=0.5, height=1.2, color=RED, fill_opacity=0.9).move_to(earth.get_center() + 0.6 * DOWN)
stage.play(FadeIn(earth), FadeIn(magnet_s), FadeIn(magnet_n))
stage.add(earth, magnet_s, magnet_n)
stage.label(earth, "geographic North", direction=UP)

beats.intent: Field lines looping from the southern end round to the northern end outside the Earth
beats.narration: Its field lines loop out of the south and back in at the north.
beats.code:
c = earth.get_center()
loops = VGroup(*[ArcBetweenPoints(c + 2.2 * DOWN, c + 2.2 * UP, angle=s * a, color=YELLOW, stroke_width=3) for s in (1, -1) for a in (PI * 0.6, PI * 0.9)])
stage.play(LaggedStart(*[Create(l) for l in loops], lag_ratio=0.2))
stage.add(loops)

beats.intent: A compass needle beside the Earth lining up along the field, its red north end pointing up
beats.narration: A compass needle is a tiny magnet, free to turn. It lines up along the field, and its north-seeking end points towards the Arctic.
beats.code:
needle = VGroup(Triangle(color=RED, fill_opacity=1).scale(0.25).stretch(2.2, 1).shift(0.3 * UP),
                Triangle(color=GREY_B, fill_opacity=1).scale(0.25).stretch(2.2, 1).rotate(PI).shift(0.3 * DOWN)).move_to([3.0, -0.3, 0]).rotate(-PI / 2)
dial = Circle(radius=1.0, color=WHITE).move_to([3.0, -0.3, 0])
stage.play(Create(dial), FadeIn(needle))
stage.play(Rotate(needle, PI / 2, about_point=dial.get_center()))
stage.add(dial, needle)
stage.label(dial, "N", direction=UP, color=RED)

beats.intent: The Earth's buried magnet labelled S at the top and N at the bottom, the needle's N end pointing to the S
beats.narration: Opposite poles attract, so the magnet pole under the geographic North is really a south pole. That's why the needle's north end is pulled there.
beats.code:
stage.add(Text("S", font_size=30, color=WHITE).move_to(magnet_s))
stage.play(FadeIn(Text("N", font_size=30, color=WHITE).move_to(magnet_n)), Indicate(magnet_s))
stage.caption("opposite poles attract: the needle's N seeks the Earth's S")

request: why is a parallelogram's area base times height?

beats.intent: A leaning parallelogram with base 5 and height 3
beats.narration: Here is a parallelogram with base five and height three.
beats.code:
stage.title("Parallelogram area")
P = [(-3, -1.5), (2, -1.5), (3.5, 1.5), (-1.5, 1.5)]
para = draw_polygon(stage, P, color=BLUE, fill=0.4)
stage.label((-0.5, -1.5), "base 5", direction=DOWN)
h = draw_line(stage, (-1.5, 1.5), (-1.5, -1.5), color=YELLOW, dashed=True)
stage.label(h, "height 3", direction=LEFT, color=YELLOW)

beats.intent: The triangle on the left cut off along the height line and shaded orange
beats.narration: Cut off the triangle on the left, along the height line.
beats.code:
tri = Polygon([-3, -1.5, 0], [-1.5, -1.5, 0], [-1.5, 1.5, 0], color=ORANGE, fill_opacity=0.7)
stage.play(FadeIn(tri))
stage.add(tri)

beats.intent: The triangle sliding to the right end, making a 5 by 3 rectangle
beats.narration: Slide it across to the other end. It fits exactly, making a rectangle.
beats.code:
stage.play(tri.animate.shift(5 * RIGHT), run_time=1.5)
rect = Rectangle(width=5, height=3, color=GREEN).move_to([1.0, 0, 0])
stage.play(Create(rect))
stage.add(rect)

beats.intent: The rectangle beside A = base × height = 5 × 3 = 15
beats.narration: Same pieces, same area: base times height, fifteen.

request: what's the chance of rolling a double with two dice?

beats.intent: The 6 by 6 grid of two-dice outcomes
beats.narration: Two dice give thirty six equally likely outcomes.

beats.intent: The six doubles on the diagonal lit: (1,1) to (6,6)
beats.narration: The doubles lie on the diagonal: one-one, two-two, up to six-six. Six of them.
beats.code:
grid = cells[0] if isinstance(cells, (tuple, list)) else cells
for k in range(6):
    stage.play(grid[k * 7].animate.set_fill(YELLOW, opacity=0.7), run_time=0.2)
stage.caption("6 doubles")

beats.narration: Six out of thirty six is one in six.

beats.intent: Another way: the first die can be anything, the second must match: 1 × 1/6
beats.narration: Or think of it this way: whatever the first die shows, the second has a one in six chance of matching it.
beats.code:
stage.equation(r"1 \times \frac16 = \frac16")
stage.caption("the second die just has to match")

request: how does drinking through a straw actually work?

beats.intent: A glass of juice with a straw, air pressure arrows pressing down on the surface
beats.narration: The air is always pressing down on the juice's surface.
beats.code:
stage.title("How a straw works")
glass = Rectangle(width=2.6, height=3.4, color=WHITE).move_to([0, -1.0, 0])
juice = Rectangle(width=2.6, height=2.4, stroke_width=0, fill_color=ORANGE, fill_opacity=0.5).align_to(glass, DOWN)
straw = Rectangle(width=0.3, height=4.4, color=GREY_B).move_to([0.4, -0.3, 0])
stage.play(Create(glass), FadeIn(juice), Create(straw))
stage.add(glass, juice, straw)
top = juice.get_top()[1]
press = VGroup(*[Arrow([x, top + 1.2, 0], [x, top + 0.1, 0], buff=0, color=BLUE) for x in (-0.9, -0.3)])
stage.play(*[GrowArrow(a) for a in press])
stage.add(press)
stage.label(press, "air pushes down", direction=LEFT, color=BLUE)

beats.intent: Air being sucked out of the top of the straw, fewer air dots inside it
beats.narration: When you suck, you remove air from the straw, so less air presses on the juice inside it.
beats.code:
out = Arrow([0.4, 2.2, 0], [0.4, 3.0, 0], buff=0, color=GREY_B)
stage.play(GrowArrow(out))
stage.add(out)
stage.label(out, "suck: less air inside", direction=RIGHT)

beats.intent: The juice rising up the straw, pushed by the outside air
beats.narration: The outside air, still pushing hard, shoves juice up the straw. You don't pull the juice: the air pushes it.
beats.code:
col = Rectangle(width=0.26, height=0.1, stroke_width=0, fill_color=ORANGE, fill_opacity=0.8).move_to([0.4, top, 0], aligned_edge=DOWN)
stage.add(col)
stage.play(col.animate.stretch_to_fit_height(2.05, about_edge=DOWN), run_time=2)
stage.caption("the air pushes the juice up")

beats.intent: The picture beside: air pressure outside > pressure inside the straw
beats.narration: It all comes down to a pressure difference: higher outside, lower inside.
